title: High Availability, Fault Tolerance, and DR

questions.prompt: What is the difference between RTO and RPO?

options.text: RTO is the maximum acceptable downtime; RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss (in time)
RTO is data loss; RPO is downtime

questions.explanation: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) is how long recovery may take; RPO (Recovery Point Objective) is how much data loss is acceptable, measured as time since the last usable copy.

questions.prompt: Order the four DR strategies from cheapest/slowest to costliest/fastest recovery.
questions.explanation: Cost and readiness rise from Backup & Restore (cheapest, slowest) through Pilot Light and Warm Standby to Multi-Site Active/Active (costliest, near-zero RTO/RPO).

questions.prompt: How is high availability usually achieved on AWS?

options.text: By running everything in a single Availability Zone
By spreading across multiple AZs with load balancing, auto scaling, and Multi-AZ databases
By using a larger single server

questions.explanation: HA removes single points of failure by spreading across multiple AZs behind a load balancer, with auto scaling and Multi-AZ databases and health checks.

questions.prompt: Why is Multi-AZ within one Region NOT enough to protect against a Region-wide outage?

options.text: It is enough — Multi-AZ covers Region failures too
Multi-AZ covers failures within a Region; a whole-Region event needs a cross-Region DR strategy

questions.explanation: HA across AZs handles failures inside one Region. A Region-wide disaster requires disaster recovery that spans Regions (replication, failover).

questions.prompt: Having more than one of a component so the loss of one doesn't stop the system is called ____.
questions.explanation: Redundancy — multiple copies of a component — is the foundation of high availability and removing single points of failure.

questions.prompt: A workload needs near-zero downtime and near-zero data loss across Regions, cost aside. Which DR strategy fits?
questions.explanation: Multi-Site Active/Active runs full production in multiple Regions simultaneously, giving near-zero RTO/RPO at the highest cost — appropriate when downtime and data loss must be minimal.
